thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'nebula-enterprise-prod' reporting GPU utilization 99% and queueing >120s (>=90% for 6m). paging oncall.
luke-sre: acked, oncall. looking now.
maria-eng: grabbing metrics, what model/tenant? I see tenant_id=nebula-corp, pool=dedicated-us-west-2-nebula
luke-sre: confirmed. single-tenant dedicated pool, traffic spike from long-context chat endpoints. KV cache heat up + many long sequences.
ryan-support: customer CSM (jessica) messaged Nebula; they're seeing 504s and slow responses in their app.
jessica-csm: Nebula reports degraded UX for a subset of users. They're live with sales demo in 30m. high priority.
devops-mike: posting quick telemetry: avg latency token=230ms -> spiking; GPU mem at 100% on 3/3 nodes; OOM logs on node-2: `cuda out of memory`.
luke-sre: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-pool-gpu-pressure
luke-sre: immediate options: 1) grant burst (if policy allows) to spin additional burst nodes 2) evict low-priority non-interactive jobs 3) enable cross-tenant overflow (not available for single-tenant dedicated) 4) instruct customer to reduce seq_len / use smaller model variant
maria-eng: quick probe: model variant is redwood/openchat-70b-unquant, seq_len distribution has 95th at 10k tokens. can we fallback to 70b-16k-quant or 13b for demo traffic?
prod-ops: we have a pre-approved burst window (nebula contract) but requires manual approval from sales ops or CS for >15m.
jessica-csm: I approve burst for 45m to get them through demo. confirming Nebula ok with potential slight cost.
luke-sre: oncall decision: try burst + evict background retraining jobs (identified job_ids: 7891, 7892) to free memory. fallback plan: if burst fails, throttle inference concurrency per-tenant.
devops-mike: kicking eviction script now: `./ops/evict-low-priority --jobs 7891,7892 --force`
devops-mike: eviction completed, freed ~26GB on each node. memory still high but not saturated.
incident-bot: deploy-bot triggered: provisioning 2x burst instances in us-west-2 (p3dn -> p4d mix) - expected ready in ~90s.
luke-sre: while waiting, enabling prefix-KV cache eviction to reduce working set for long-chats: `cache:policy=aggressive`.
maria-eng: rolling traffic rule: route new demo requests to quantized variant `openchat-70b-q4_0` for demo path `/nebula/demo`. patching routing rule now.
prod-ops: burst nodes are up. GPUs reporting 12% free mem buffer, schedulers accepting queued requests.
ryan-support: Nebula reports improvement, latency dropping to ~420ms and no more 504s for demo users.
jessica-csm: Nebula product lead says demo looks good. thanks team.
luke-sre: monitoring for next 20m. action items: 1) follow up with Nebula on seq_len / prompt truncation best practices 2) evaluate model variant recommendations 3) check autoscale thresholds for dedicated pool (increase baseline?)
maria-eng: note: we observed many ultra-long sequences from a small set of API keys — recommend rate limiting per-key for long-seq path.
prod-ops: we'll open a capacity review with infra to consider autoscaling policy tweak and burst SLA wording for Nebula contract.
jessica-csm: I'll coordinate customer comms and record the timeline.
oncall-rotation: handoff to night oncall at 1777778905 — luke will do 5m overlap and then create follow-up ticket.
luke-sre: creating incident ticket and postmortem stub: https://redwood.internal/incidents/NEBULA-1777778888
luke-sre: final note: avoided eviction of interactive sessions, used contract burst + targeted evictions + model routing to mitigate. will document cost and recommend a short-term reserved bump if Nebula can't trim seq_len.
incident-bot: incident severity updated -> Sev3 (customer visible but mitigated).
